source_text:
34 Πᾶσαν κακὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἄπωσαι ἀπό σου, καὶ οὐ μὴ λυπήσωσίν σε οἱ

ἐχθροί σου.
35 Ψάλλε ἀπὸ καρδίας σου, καὶ μὴ κίνει μόνον τὴν γλῶσσαν σου ἐν τῷ
στόματί σου.
36 Ἄφρων παρθένος ἀγαπήσει ἀργύριον, ἡ δὲ φρονίμη προσθήσει καὶ τὸν
ψωμὸν αὐτῆς.
37 Ὥσπερ ὁρμὴ πυρὸς δυσκάθεκτος, οὕτως ψυχὴ παρθένου τρωθεῖσα
δυσίατος.
38 Μὴ δώῃς τὴν ψυχήν σου διαλογισμοῖς πονηροῖς, ἵνα μὴ μιάνωσι σὴν
καρδίαν καὶ καθαρὰν προσευχὴν μακρὰν ποιήσωσι ἀπό σου.
39 Βαρεῖα λύπη καὶ ἀνυπόστατος ἀκηδία, δάκρυα δὲ πρὸς θεὸν ἰσχυρότερα
ἀμφοτέρων.
40 Λιμὸς καὶ δίψα μαραίνει ἐπιθυμίας κακάς, ἀγρυπνία δὲ ἀγαθὴ καθαίρει
διάνοιαν.
41 Ὀργὴν καὶ θυμὸν ἀποστρέφει ἀγάπη, μνησικακίαν δὲ ἀνατρέπει δῶρα.
42 Ἡ καταλαλοῦσα λάθρα τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς ἐξωσθήσεται τοῦ νυμφῶνος,
καὶ βοήσεται πρὸς ταῖς θύραις αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ὑπακούων.
43 Παρθένου ἀνελεήμονος σβεσθήσεται λαμπάς, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδῃ προελθόντα
τὸν νυμφίον αὐτῆς.
44 Ὕαλος προσπίπτων λίθῳ συντριβήσεται, καὶ παρθένος ἁπτομένη ἀνδρὸς
οὐκ ἀθωωθήσεται.
45 Κρείσσων γυνὴ πραεῖα παρθένου ὀργίλου καὶ θυμώδους.
46 Ἡ ἐξέλκουσα ἐν γέλωτι λόγους ἀνδρός, ὁμοία ἐστὶν τῇ περιβαλλούσῃ
βρόχον τῷ ἑαυτῆς τραχήλῳ.
47 Ὥσπερ μαργαρίτης ἐν σφενδόνῃ χρυσῇ, οὕτως παρθένος καλυπτομένη ὑπὸ
αἰδοῦς. 48 Ὠιδαὶ δαιμόνων καὶ αὐλοὶ ἐκλύουσιν ψυχὴν καὶ ἀπολλύουσιν εὐτονίαν
αὐτῆς, ἣν φύλαξον διὰ παντός, ἵνα μὴ ἐπονείδιστος γένῃ.
49 Μὴ τέρπου ἐπὶ γελοίοις, καὶ ἐπισκωπτούσαις μὴ εὐφραίνου, ὅτι κύριος
ἐγκατέλιπεν αὐτάς.
thought_title: Guarding the virgin's soul from desire, sorrow, and defilement
orientation: Evagrius continues his series of short counsels to the consecrated virgin, warning her against desires, evil thoughts, and the dangers that can quench her lamp and bar her from the bridal chamber.
pass_a_gloss: Every evil desire push away from yourself, and your enemies will not grieve you. Sing from your heart, and do not move only your tongue in your mouth. A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will give also her morsel. As a rush of fire is hard to check, so the soul of a wounded virgin is hard to heal. Do not give your soul to evil thoughts, so that they may not defile your heart and make pure prayer far from you. Heavy grief and unbearable spiritual apathy, but tears toward God are stronger than both. Hunger and thirst wither evil desires, and good vigil purifies the mind. Anger and wrath love turns away, and resentment gifts overturn. She who slanders her sister secretly will be thrust out of the bridal chamber, and she will cry at its doors and there will be no one listening. Of a merciless virgin the lamp will be quenched, and she will not see her bridegroom coming forth. Glass falling against a stone will be shattered, and a virgin touching a man will not be acquitted. Better is a gentle woman than an angry and wrathful virgin. She who draws out in laughter the words of a man is like one putting a noose around her own neck. As a pearl in a golden setting, so is a virgin covered by modesty. Songs of demons and flutes weaken the soul and destroy its vigor, which guard at all times, so that you may not become reproached. Do not delight in jokes, and do not rejoice with mocking women, because the Lord has abandoned them.

choices.why: Glossary term for listlessness or spiritual torpor; renders the oppressive state of soul Evagrius names.
Glossary term for the place of union with Christ; keeps the nuptial imagery of the parable.
Glossary term for the lamp of the virgin soul; preserves the Gospel parable imagery.
Glossary term for the mind or understanding purified by vigil and prayer.
Glossary term for tempting or evil thoughts that defile the heart.
Glossary term for pure and constant prayer.

bible_refs.note: The lamp, oil, bridegroom, and bridal chamber imagery in sections 42-43 draws on the parable of the ten virgins.

pass_b_english: Push away every evil desire from yourself, and your enemies will not grieve you.
Sing from your heart, and do not merely move your tongue in your mouth.
A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread.
As a rush of fire is hard to quench, so the soul of a wounded virgin is hard to heal.
Do not hand your soul over to wicked thoughts, lest they defile your heart and drive pure prayer far from you.
Heavy grief and unbearable spiritual apathy—but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.
Hunger and thirst wither evil desires, and a good vigil purifies the mind.
Love turns away anger and rage, and gifts overturn resentment.
The one who secretly slanders her sister will be thrust out of the bridal chamber, and she will cry out at its doors, and there will be no one to answer.
The lamp of a merciless virgin will be quenched, and she will not see her bridegroom when he comes forth.
Glass struck by a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be held guiltless.
A gentle woman is better than an angry and wrathful virgin.
The one who draws out a man's words with laughter is like one who fastens a noose around her own neck.
As a pearl in a golden setting, so is a virgin veiled by modesty.
Songs of demons and flutes weaken the soul and destroy its vigor; guard this at all times, lest you become a reproach.
Do not delight in jokes, and do not rejoice with those who mock, for the Lord has abandoned them.

problems.quote: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the wise one will give away even her own morsel of bread.
problems.source_quote: Ἄφρων παρθένος ἀγαπήσει ἀργύριον, ἡ δὲ φρονίμη προσθήσει καὶ τὸν ψωμὸν αὐτῆς.
problems.why: Greek says the prudent virgin will add her own bread (προσθήσει), not give it away.
problems.fix: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own bread.

problems.quote: Glass that strikes a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be held guiltless.
problems.source_quote: Ὕαλος προσπίπτων λίθῳ συντριβήσεται, καὶ παρθένος ἁπτομένη ἀνδρὸς οὐκ ἀθωωθήσεται.
problems.why: Greek says the glass is shattered when struck by a stone; English reverses the agency.
problems.fix: Glass struck by a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be made innocent.

problems.why: ἀνυπόστατος means 'insubstantial, without foundation' not 'unbearable'; the grief and apathy lack substance/are groundless, not intolerable.
English adds 'are strong' not in source; source says tears are stronger than both, not that grief and apathy are strong.
problems.fix: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy—but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.
problems.ruling: adds 'are strong' for grief/apathy not in source

problems.why: English adds 'are strong' to describe grief and apathy, but source only says tears are stronger than both.
problems.fix: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy—but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.
problems.ruling: adds 'are strong' not present in Greek

edits.old: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the wise one will give away even her own morsel of bread.
edits.new: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread.

edits.old: Glass that strikes a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be held guiltless.
edits.new: Glass struck by a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be held guiltless.

edits.old: Heavy grief and unbearable spiritual apathy are strong, but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.
edits.new: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy—but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.

fixed: Changed 'wise one' to 'prudent one' and 'give away' to 'add' to match προσθήσει (she adds her own bread, not gives it away).
Changed 'Glass that strikes a stone' to 'Glass struck by a stone' to match the Greek passive sense (προσπίπτων λίθῳ = falling against a stone, i.e., struck by it).
Changed 'unbearable' to 'groundless' for ἀνυπόστατος (without substance/foundation), and removed the added 'are strong' to match the source, which only says tears are stronger than both.

problems.quote: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy
problems.why: Here ἀνυπόστατος means "unbearable" or "irresistible" (matching "heavy" and "stronger than both"), not "groundless"; the Greek is also a full clause, not a fragment.
problems.fix: Grief is heavy and spiritual apathy is unbearable
problems.ruling: ἀνυπόστατος means unbearable/unresistible, not groundless; misstates ἀκηδία and breaks parallel with βαρεῖα and ἰσχυρότερα ἀμφοτέρων.

edits.old: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy
edits.new: Heavy grief and unbearable spiritual apathy

fixed: Heavy grief and groundless spiritual apathy: ἀνυπόστατος means unbearable, not groundless — restored unbearable; Greek has no verb so kept the nominal phrasing.

last_rejected.quote: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἄφρων παρθένος ἀγαπήσει ἀργύριον, ἡ δὲ φρονίμη προσθήσει καὶ τὸν ψωμὸν αὐτῆς.
last_rejected.why: ἀγαπήσει is future 'will love,' but προσθήσει means 'will add'—to what? The sense requires 'will add [money to buy] even her own morsel,' i.e., she'll sell even her bread for alms. 'Add even her own morsel' is nonsensical; the prudent virgin gives/sacrifices her bread.
last_rejected.fix: A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread [to her giving].
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says ἀγαπήσει ἀργύριον, προσθήσει τὸν ψωμὸν αὐτῆς; translation 'will love silver' and 'will add her own bread' matches.

last_rejected.quote: The one who draws out a man's words with laughter
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἡ ἐξέλκουσα ἐν γέλωτι λόγους ἀνδρός
last_rejected.why: ἐξέλκουσα means 'drawing out, extracting'—the virgin is eliciting/flattering words from the man, not 'drawing out a man's words with laughter' as if the words contain laughter. She uses laughter to draw him out.
last_rejected.fix: She who draws out a man's words with laughter
last_rejected.ruling: Greek Ἡ ἐξέλκουσα ἐν γέλωτι λόγους ἀνδρός = 'she who extracts a man's words with laughter'; translation reflects this.

last_rejected.quote: As a rush of fire is hard to quench, so the soul of a wounded virgin is hard to heal.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὥσπερ ὁρμὴ πυρὸς δυσκάθεκτος, οὕτως ψυχὴ παρθένου τρωθεῖσα δυσίατος.
last_rejected.why: τρωθεῖσα means ‘being devoured/consumed’, not ‘wounded’; the sense of the soul being consumed by hardship is lost.
last_rejected.fix: As a rush of fire is hard to quench, so the soul of a virgin being devoured by hardship is hard to satisfy.
last_rejected.ruling: τρωθεῖσα is passive of τιτρώσκω, 'wound/pierce'; 'wounded' is correct, not 'devoured'.

last_rejected.quote: but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread.
last_rejected.why: προσθήσει here means 'will give away' or 'will offer'; 'will add' leaves no object to add to and obscures the contrast with loving silver.
last_rejected.fix: but the prudent one will give away even her own morsel of bread.
last_rejected.ruling: προσθήσει allows 'add/contribute'; καὶ τὸν ψωμὸν αὐτῆς names what she adds; contrast with ἀργύριον remains.
